data.standardized_narrative: Opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2019 were GBP 743.465m. A reassessment of older underwriting years (2016 & prior) produced a gross improvement of GBP 38.0m, driven by favourable claims development on the back years. The movement represents a ~5.1% release relative to opening gross claims. Notable loss events mentioned across current and prior years include aviation losses (Lion Air and Ethiopian Airlines), Hurricane Dorian and 2018 catastrophe activity (California wildfires, Hurricanes Florence and Michael), but the overall prior year reserve movement reported was a favourable release primarily attributed to reserve development rather than a single event.
raw_causal_phrases: Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2016 & prior (2018 - 2015 & prior) resulted in an improvement of GBP 38.0m (2018 - GBP 44.6m).
The syndicate has continued to benefit from favourable development on the back years, contributing a saving of 8% on the loss ratio (2018 - 10%).
There was a lower incidence of catastrophe losses in 2019 with Hurricane Dorian contributing 2% to the loss ratio for the year.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Balance Sheet 'Claims outstanding' prior-year column. Prior year development (GBP 38.0m improvement) taken from Note 6 narrative which explicitly states the gross improvement for underwriting years 2016 & prior. The claims development triangle (gross) is present and provided as cross-check. Some event-specific amounts (e.g. Hurricane Dorian reserve ~ $11m; gross aviation reserves GBP 21.2m) are reported in currencies or as gross reserves; where net GBP-quantified losses are not explicitly stated in GBP, amounts are left null. No per-line-of-business gross prior-year reserve movements were provided.
